mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a -2% y/y drop in INDPRO, indicating the supply shock is not impacting equity prices as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as a 0.5 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating the labor market deterioration is not impacting consumer behavior as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate, defined as a 1 percentage point increase over the past 6 months, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 1pp hike in FEDFUNDS over 6 months, indicating the tightening is not impacting equity prices as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, as measured by the year-over-year change in the HOUST index, signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks (ITB ETF) outperform the broader market by > 2% over the 20-day signal period, indicating the housing market weakness is not impacting related equities as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the consumer price index, as measured by the year-over-year change in the CPIAUCSL index, signals rising inflation that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real yields (TIPS breakeven rates) fall by > 50bps over the 60-day signal period, indicating the inflation spike is not impacting the real cost of capital as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment, as measured by the 3-month change in the PAYEMS index, signals a strengthening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (Advance Retail Sales index) fall by > 1% over the 20-day signal period, indicating the labor market strength is not translating into consumer spending as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in real estate loans, as measured by the 3-month change in the RSAFS index, signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Mortgage rates (30-year fixed) rise by > 50bps over the 20-day signal period, indicating the housing market strength is being offset by rising financing costs.
